content:
Let \(N\) be a 10-digit number, so
\[
10^9 \le N < 10^{10}.
\]
If \(N^2\) had 20 digits, then the remaining block would have \(d=10\), so
\[
N\cdot 10^{10} \le N^2 \implies N \ge 10^{10},
\]
impossible. Thus \(N^2\) has 19 digits and \(d=9\). Hence
\[
N\cdot 10^9 \le N^2 < (N+1)10^9.
\]
The first inequality is automatic since \(N\ge 10^9\). The second gives
\[
N(N-10^9) < 10^9.
\]
Let \(k=N-10^9\). Then
\[
k(10^9+k)<10^9.
\]
For \(k=0\), this holds. For \(k\ge 1\),
\[
k(10^9+k)\ge 10^9+1>10^9,
\]
so no solutions. Therefore \(k=0\), so
\[
N=10^9=1000000000.
\]
Check: \(N^2=10^{18}\), whose first 10 digits are \(1000000000\).

\[
\boxed{1000000000}
\]
